name: Graph reconstruction conjecture
question: Is each finite simple graph on at least three vertices determined by its vertex-deleted deck?
first_attack: Prove reconstruction for a new graph family
method_title: Replay the object, or mine the census
dispatch_next: Degree + triangles + induced P4 now separates the census through 6 vertices (research/M078_P4.md). At n = 7 the same triple still leaves 116 excess graphs, or 36 with C4 added. Isolate a deck-readable invariant that finishes n = 7, or a structural family where those collisions concentrate; do not enlarge the verified reconstruction range.
dispatch_why: Degree + triangles + induced P4 now separates through 6 vertices. The remaining collisions start at n = 7; enlarging the census sits inside McKay's published range.

campaign.method: Deck-collision search over certified graph censuses
campaign.hypothesis: Every finite simple graph on at least 3 vertices is determined up to isomorphism by its vertex-deleted deck.
campaign.first_proof_obligation: Pick a graph family not yet known to be reconstructible and isolate a lemma that reconstructs a new invariant for it.
campaign.next_experiment: Degree + triangles + induced P4 now separates the census through 6 vertices (research/M078_P4.md). At n = 7 the same triple still leaves 116 excess graphs, or 36 with C4 added. Isolate a deck-readable invariant that finishes n = 7, or a structural family where those collisions concentrate; do not enlarge the verified reconstruction range.
campaign.falsification: Two non-isomorphic graphs with identical decks, confirmed by independent canonical forms.
campaign.blocker: Computer verification already reaches at least 11 vertices; novelty has to come from a structural lemma, not from range.

probes.name: Graph reconstruction conjecture
probes.title: Vertex-deck reconstruction for every graph up to N vertices
probes.frontier: Known: verified by computer for all graphs on at most 11 vertices (McKay 1997) and beyond; proved for trees, regular and disconnected graphs (Kelly 1957).

smoke.scope: For every n with 3 <= n <= 6, the 6-vertex census is complete (Burnside-certified) and no two non-isomorphic graphs share a vertex-deleted deck.

deep.scope: For every n with 3 <= n <= 7, the 7-vertex census is complete (Burnside-certified) and no two non-isomorphic graphs share a vertex-deleted deck.

milestones.title: Graph reconstruction verified for every graph on 3-6 vertices
milestones.description: Burnside-certified census of 4, 11, 34 and 156 graphs; all decks pairwise distinct under an independent canonical form. Deep run adds all 1,044 graphs on 7 vertices.

milestones.title: Deck-certified degree, triangle and induced-P4 separation through 6 vertices
milestones.scope: Census already known to be reconstructible far beyond 6 vertices; this only ranks coarse invariants
milestones.description: Degree sequence separates through 4 vertices. Degree plus triangles separates through 5 and leaves 20 excess at 6. Adding the deck-readable induced P4 count finishes separation through 6. All three invariants are recomputed from cards.

formal_statement.encodes: Simple graphs on n ≥ 3 vertices with a deck-matching bijection σ (G − v ≅ H − σv) are isomorphic.
